Add a second function to the library:
[[nodiscard]] double heading_change_rad(WheelTicks ticks, const Wheels& wheels)
. It returns the change in heading in radians for a differential-drive robot, which is the right wheel's distance minus the left wheel's, divided by the distance between the wheels.
Write at least three GoogleTest cases for it: equal ticks give 0; the right wheel turning further gives a positive value; swapping the wheels changes the sign and nothing else.
Build and run everything with the three commands from the theory. Then make one test fail on purpose and read GoogleTest's message.

c.v: next to the distance tests and their
The same three checks as a plain program, so that the page's checker compiles and runs them:

The first and the third tests compare exactly. Equal ticks give a difference of 0, and 0 times anything is exactly 0. Swapping the wheels negates the difference, and rounding to nearest treats a negative number the same way as its positive twin, so every step gives exactly the negative of the other side's result. The integer type isn't what makes these exact: the same holds with

ticks. It is there so a tick count can't be confused with other numbers, and so counts above 2⁵³ stay exact. The second test multiplies and divides by 0.001 and 0.4, which have no exact binary form, so it gets a tolerance. A positive heading change is a turn to the left, counter-clockwise, which is the convention ROS uses for yaw.
